data.body:
CRITICAL FINDING from running rebar review-plan against real Bedrock (recorded on ticket 2932). Flagged here because it may make this story AC4 unpassable as written, and because I could NOT settle it with the credentials available.

THE FINDING: this plan grants bedrock:InvokeModel + bedrock:InvokeModelWithResponseStream. rebars Bedrock integration goes through pydantic-ais BedrockProvider, which calls the **Converse** API (confirmed in-repo: the measured error text in tests/unit/test_bedrock_provider.py reads when calling the Converse operation). If AWS treats bedrock:Converse / bedrock:ConverseStream as action namespaces DISTINCT from bedrock:InvokeModel, then the grant as written yields AccessDeniedException and this storys own AC — a minimal bedrock-runtime Converse call from the instance — cannot pass.

WHY I DID NOT VERIFY IT, stated plainly rather than guessed: the IAM identity available here (user joe_sec) carries AmazonBedrockFullAccess, which grants bedrock:* — a wildcard. Every Converse call I made therefore succeeded regardless of which specific action Converse requires, so my successful calls are NOT evidence either way. I am not going to assert the answer from recollection when the consequence is a production IAM grant that fails closed.

THE DECISIVE TEST, for whoever implements this story with the review-bot credentials: either (a) run  for the review-bot role against BOTH bedrock:InvokeModel and bedrock:Converse on the target model ARN, or (b) apply the scoped grant to a throwaway role and issue a real Converse call. Do NOT rely on a wildcard-holding identity to validate a scoped policy — that is precisely the setup that hides this class of error until production.

Also worth checking while in that file: the same review flagged the plans citation of infra/terraform/iam.tf:59 for the rebar-gerrit-instance-role declaration as wrong (it reads the role as declared at lines 26-33, with :59 falling inside the ssm_params_read policy body), and that infra/runbooks/ appears in Scope with no AC covering it.
